The plan is safe and it doesn't follow Marisol's idea of doubling to 80. It totals 43 mi, in line with the 40 and 53 mi weeks, and it keeps her Mon/Fri rest days and her Wednesday session. Her heavy legs had cleared by Thursday, so there's no warning sign to act on. The days are clear enough to run, with set distances and pace or heart-rate caps.

The weak spot is the answer to her question, which the rubric weighs heavily. The draft never plainly says no to 80 miles or to running twice a day. It doesn't explain that doubling her volume in one week is a real injury risk, and it doesn't say that her club mate's 70 miles took time to build. The reason it gives, "adding extra miles without hard work can backfire," is muddled and doesn't make sense.

There are also mismatches. The summary calls Sunday a "moderate long run," but 20 mi is nearly half the week. The card doesn't give her recent long-run lengths, so whether 20 is a big jump can't be checked. Wednesday is called "threshold work," but the workout is marathon pace. Overall it's a safe, usable plan with a weak reply to the one thing she asked.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 24, 27, 37, 53 mi
This week: 40 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs a bit heavy early in the week, fine by Thursday."
Asks: "My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Keep the single hard day, add a moderate long run, and stay within the plan to stay on track for a sub-3:45 finish.
Answers: You did well, but keep mileage at planned levels. Adding extra miles without hard work can backfire.
Next week:
Mon: rest
Tue: easy, 5 mi, keep HR under 150, flat route. Loosens legs after long run.
Wed: quality, 8 mi, 5 mi at marathon pace, warm-up easy, focuses on threshold work.
Thu: easy, 6 mi, 9:45–10:00 pace, maintain low HR 140–145, active recovery.
Fri: rest
Sat: easy, 4 mi, very light, keep HR < 140, promotes recovery.
Sun: long, 20 mi, easy pace, HR under 150, adds volume but stays easy.
